app_info.detailed_description:
Wishlist our new game


Roadmap


About the Game

Dorfromantik is a relaxing building strategy and puzzle game in which you place tiles to create ever-growing, idyllic village landscapes. With Dorfromantik, you can immerse yourself in a quiet, peaceful world at any time and take a break from everyday life. At the same time, Dorfromantik offers a challenge for those who are looking for one: To beat the highscore, you need to carefully plan and strategically place your tiles.



In Dorfromantik you start with a stack of procedurally generated tiles. One after the other, you draw the top tile of the stack, place it on one available slot and rotate for the best fit. Thereby groups and combinations of landscapes are formed, such as forests, villages or water bodies, and you are rewarded with points depending on how well the tile fits.



On some tiles you will also encounter special objects that give you a quest: For example, the windmill wants to border 6 grain fields, the locomotive wants to be connected to 10 tracks or the deer wants to inhabit a forest with at least 50 trees. Fulfill these quests to get more tiles to continue the expansion of your landscape. The game ends when the tile stack is used up.

As you expand the landscape, you can advance into new, colorful biomes and discover pre-placed game objects that give you long-term tasks. Through these tasks you can unlock new tiles, new biomes and new quests.



What Dorfromantik offers

  • Building endless and beautiful landscapes
  • Unique mix of strategy and puzzle mechanics
  • Relaxing and calming gameplay
  • Idyllic village scenery
  • Strategic placement to beat the highscore
  • High replay value - every session is different
  • Many unlockable tiles and biomes
  • Original Artstyle with handpainted boardgame feel

What Dorfromantik does not offer

  • 4X Strategy
  • Trading
  • Resource Management
  • Combat & Violence
  • Multiplayer



Dorfromantik offers options for any style of play! Take a short break from life in quick mode or try to master the game in hard mode. The Custom Mode allows you to create your own rulesets and share them with others, while monthly mode awaits you with a new challenge every month. If you just want to relax and build your own landscape with no limits, try the creative mode!





Dorfromantik was developed by four game design students from Berlin. Together we have founded Toukana Interactive and want to develop many more small, original and high-quality indie games in the future.

We are happy about constructive feedback of all kinds, so feel free to contact us! We will do our best to respond to messages quickly and fix any problems that may arise. :)

[h1]Peaceful tile game. Made me question whether knowledge is real. 10/10.[/h1]
 
[b]It's genuinely good.[/b]
Visually soothing. Strategically satisfying. Deep enough to reward long-term play. No time pressure, no punishment, just vibes and planning. Hex tiles and gentle music: the gateway drug of digital peace.
I started playing Dorfromantik for the same reason everyone does: it’s relaxing, charming, and makes you feel clever without punishing you.
Then I played a bit more.
And more.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]But then I started thinking [spoiler](big mistake)[/spoiler][/h3]
The game gives you tiles, each with six sides. each side has one of six terrain types: house, field, forest, etc. I started thinking about the combinatorics of tile placement. The more tiles you place the more edge, and, therefore, potential options you get.
I asked: [i]How many tiles do I need to place before it’s mathematically guaranteed that any random tile will have a perfect spot on the board?[/i]

And I found the number. 7,826 (Give or take, depending on constraints. I used Dirichlet polynomial enumeration.)

[h3]And then everything got weird[/h3]
At tile 7,826, the system becomes [i]complete[/i]. Every possible combination exists somewhere. You are guaranteed to find a perfect fit for any tile.

Then you place it.

And suddenly, for tile 7,827, that mathematical guarantee vanishes.

[b][i]Why?[/i][/b]
 
How the more tiles you place the higher the probability to find a perfect match, but then once the system is probibalistically complete it collapses into the uncertainty again? Does certainty truly exist if it vanishes the moment it becomes real?

That’s when Dorfromantik stopped being a game and became a meditation on certainty, information, and reality itself.

Is it possible to “know” something is true if realizing it changes the truth conditions? From there, I fell into quantum mechanics, Gödel's incompleteness, and the limits of Bayesian inference. Because if your model assumes the outcome is already determined, but the system is fundamentally indeterminate, is probability truely is just a model of ignorance, or does it shape the world it predicts?

Just like in the game: the tile doesn’t “reveal” a match, it defines it. Placement collapses the space of possibility into one specific configuration. Probability becomes destiny. But only once. Then it resets.

[i]What does it mean to know something before it happens?
Can a guarantee exist if acting on it makes it disappear?
Is certainty a thing that lives in potential but dies in realization?[/i]

 [hr][/hr]
[b]The game didn’t give me answers.[/b]

Just fields, rivers, windmills, and a slowly expanding floor full of beautiful, subtle existential dread.

[b]10/10. Would recommend. Just maybe don’t play it at 3AM while thinking about the fragility of epistemic foundations, Gödel and quantum indeterminacy.[/b]

I've noticed I haven't reviewed this game. Well, the hour count speaks for itself. I used to run it without thinking much (and therefore never unlocked "infinite" mode) while listening to podcasts and it took that amount of hours to finally get tired of it, so yeah, totally recommended.

It's fun and all but it will use your autism and/or OCD against you, any semblance of logic or aesthetic will be punished; you WILL build a railway that goes nowhere and you WILL build random bursts of vegetation in the middle of a wheat field.

I don't know if there's a proper word for it, but this game is a perfect minor stimulus that serves as a vessel for thinking and reflecting. It's like the feeling you get when you're on a walk, where you have some small task (putting one foot in front of the other) that keeps you lightly engaged while your brain is free to wander and think about other things.

📖 - Game Genre: Cozy Puzzle / Tile Placement / Chill Strategy
⌚ - Session Length: Ideal for short bursts or extended zoning out (15 min to hours)
🧬 - Game DNA: Carcassonne + Islanders + A Good Spotify Playlist
💰 ROI: 9.52 / 38.9 = $0.24 per hour


This is a pretty simple game. You start with a stack of terrain tiles and on each tile there are a few different terrain types: field, forest, houses, farms, rivers, railroads. Your job is to place them next to each other while trying to match the terrain on each tile with the terrain of it's neighbors. If you match each side perfectly, you get 100 points as well as a bonus for any completed tiles around it. There are also quests to add a specific number of terrain types in a connected line. You get points if you complete them, as well as a number of new tiles.  You keep doing this until you are out of tiles, so as you can see the more quests and perfect matches you have, the longer you go and the higher your score.

It sounds easy, but it's really not. It get's really hard to find a final perfect piece for an open spot. Also, you need to be aware of when the game is going to end and how to maximize your points as your tiles run out. It's very easy to block yourself in.

What's good about it? 
[list]
[*]It's very relaxing. There is no clock or move limit, so you can move pieces around the board to find the perfect spot. 
[*]The "one more turn" factor is super high. I've lost hours playing this game.
[*]The game has nice aids that help you see thing easier, which is good for my old eyes. When you place a piece on the board but before clicks to finalize your placement, the sides of the piece that match it's neighbors will highlight so you can easily see if it's a perfect match. Also, some quests require you to "close" the connectable edges of a previous quest, and the game will highlight the remaining edges the need to be closed with a non-similar terrain tile, or at least one that doesn't carry the pattern further.
[/list]

What didn't I like?
[list]
[*]The one more turn factor means I stay up too late playing. I'm old and I need my sleep. This game is anti-sleep medicine.
[*]Sometimes the piece highlighting is wonky and you have to rotate the camera to see if an edge is actually highlighted or not. Also, when you have a quest to close an area, the water is light blue. The map background is a similar color. This means that to close blue, you often have to use your brain to figure out which edges still need to be close, or you are going to spend a lot of time asking "is that also light blue? Did the color change?:
[*]I don't really understand the unlocks. You can earn pieces by completing achievements, and also maybe by building to a hidden tile on the map and connecting to it. But I don't know what it means to have these tiles unlocked. Does it mean they have a chance to appear in the game now? Because I unlocked a bever dam and only saw it in one game. 

That's reallly about it. This game is a huge time-suck. One of the things I really enjoy is just looking at the map after I finish. During the game you get little snapshots of your land, but for me it's very satisfying to scroll around and see where the fields turn to a small town, or where two little houses are connected deep in the forest, or where I played a little lake in the middle of a field. I really love this game and it is quickly raising up to a Balatro\Dave the Diver\Cult of the Lamb status of games that are going to be in my rotation for a long time.

I do like this game but there is one flaw: no matter how well you play, you will ALWAYS lose because sooner or later (even if a lot later) you will run out of cards... and no matter how many points you have, it still sux and you will still end the game with a feeling of losing.
Yes there is free play but that takes the game out of it. So if the devs want to make this game even better, maybe have a wild card option? Or maybe throughout the game, when you hit certain points you get to "purchase" a small stack of new cards..? 
Anyway; the game is still worth even if they don't add this, but it would lengthen the playability (because I am getting tired of the "losing" feeling no matter how well I play)

When you first start playing, Dorfromantik is a chill, relaxing puzzle game that you can play for a few hours. If you keep playing, it's an infinite jigsaw that never runs out of pieces. If either sound appealing, you'll like this game.

In recent years there have been a lot of simple, gentle farming and management games, or even just creative design games that seem primarily geared toward good vibes and calm atmosphere. Almost across the board, these games don't work for me. The lack of goals or conflict make everything feel a bit perfunctory, and the creation elements are not very motivating since there is often no way to interact with your creations meaningfully. 

Dorfromantik, though, is a game for people like me. It still has the calming music and pleasant visuals, the lack of time constraints or action mechanics, and the overall low stakes of those other games, but with a clear general goal (lay tiles in the best combinations to score points and add more tiles to your deck), and the threat of your deck actually running out and your session coming to an end. The reason this doesn't feel too tense is that the game mostly just plays like a high score chaser with some permanent progression and new cosmetic unlocks and goals to achieve for their own sake. It's a good middle solution for people who want to chill out without forgoing traditional gameplay entirely, and one I recommend.

Quite literally my comfort game. As a master's student, this game has kept me sane and cured my ails.
Headache? Dorfromantik.
Depressed? Dorfromantik.
Burnout? Dorfromantik.

[b]Dorfromantik[/b] is a cozy tile-placement game that pairs well with an audiobook or existential dread.  It took me 82 hours to 100%, and I wouldn't describe the experience as "fun" so much as the mental equivalent of a hot stone massage.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
Gameplay revolves around drawing and placing tiles one-by-one, and the goal is to score as many points as possible before you run out of tiles.  Each procedurally-generated hexagonal tile features some combination of terrain types, and scores 10 points for each edge that matches the terrain of an adjacent tile, plus an extra 60 points if all edges match.  Some include "missions" that require you to chain a certain quantity of terrain, and score more points (plus more tiles!) when completed.  (You have to manually count houses and fields, but thankfully not trees.) 

[b]Controls.[/b]  Playable with mouse/keyboard, controller, and Deck.  Controls are intuitive and familiar on all three.

[b]Playtime.[/b]  In "classic mode," a round can run anywhere from 10 minutes to hours; it all depends on how you play.  My longest round was ~6 hours, but also required a lot of deliberation because I [i]needed[/i] that "Heavy Weight VII" achievement.  You can save at any time, close, and pick up where you left off, and can have saves for every mode. 

[b]Modes.[/b]  Alternate game modes include "Creative Mode," which is basically a stress-free diorama builder; "Hard Mode," which has fewer missions; a quick game that has a set number of tiles; and monthly challenges with predetermined seeds.   

⚠️ [b]Achievements.[/b]  It's easy to assume achievements are bugged when you don't receive "Farmer I" for your first massive field, but they're actually tied to in-game "Challenges" that are slowly unlocked as you play.  If the challenge isn't unlocked, you can't score the achievement. 

[h3]What Works For Me[/h3]
✅ [b]Graphics.[/b]  This game is gorgeous: between the color palette, hand-drawn tiles, and animated little boats and trains, every world you build feels picturesque.  Completing challenges unlocks new terrain "skins" which randomly add variety and life to the board; e.g. one region might feature a sunny asian-inspired town while the other side of the board is clearly celebrating Halloween.

✅ [b]Sound Design.[/b]  The music is tranquil, and the various sound effects include trains, birds, and farm noises (which admittedly can be a bit annoying).  There are separate sliders for Master, Music, and FX volumes.  I liked what I listened to, but honestly switched to audiobooks and podcasts some ~60 hours ago. 

✅ [b]Tile Placement.[/b]  Whether we're talking board games or digital, tile placement is one of my favorite mechanics and [i]strategic[/i] tile placement is like catnip to me.  [b]Dorf[/b] does this well: as your board expands and stack shrinks, picking the perfect place for a tile becomes increasingly tricky. 

[h3]What Doesn't Work For Me[/h3]
❎  [b]Simplicity.[/b]  The combination of simple gameplay and repetition is relaxing, and the game can be quite difficult at times (especially in context of "Puzzler" and "Heavy Weight" challenges), but there's no crunch or complexity or hidden layers here: it promises simple tile placement and that's exactly what it delivers.   As a result, it's hard for me to play after completing the challenges.

[h3]Final Thoughts[/h3]
The first time I played [b]Dorfromantik[/b], six hours vanished in the blink of an eye and I walked away feeling strangely settled… but also told my husband, "I don't think this is fun."   Even now, when I talk about [b]Dorf[/b], it invariably sounds like a hostage situation.

For me, it's not fun.  It doesn't make me happy. 

What it does make me feel is [i]zen[/i].  It's been a stressful few years on all fronts, and playing a round or two of [b]Dorf[/b] has been as effective as therapy or a massage for me; I can sit at my desk, zone out, and mindlessly place tiles and soak in pretty sights while the stress melts away… or at least packs itself up for a while.  (Note: Not an appropriate substitute for therapy.)

[h3]Recommendation[/h3]
Do you want to relax, place tiles, and create pretty landscapes?  If yes, [b]Dorf[/b] is absolutely worth your time and whatever you pay for it. 

If you want a tile-placement city-building game that feels like more of a challenge, then I'd try [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2485350/River_Towns/?curator_clanid=45365863]River Towns[/url] or [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2525310/Drop_Duchy/?curator_clanid=45365863]Drop Duchy[/url] instead. 

[quote][b]Follow [u][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45365863/]Eekz Today[/url][/u] for more crafting, life sim, management, strategy, and story-rich recommendations.[/b][/quote]

[h1]PROS: [/h1]

➕Chill music


[h1]CONS: [/h1]
➖I wish the game would tell you why you can’t place a tile in a specific place
➖Not a lot of depth/Heavy RNG based

[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
The game world starts off with a blank slate of nothingness with a single hexagon tile in the middle. You then create the game world through hexagons with different layouts like forests, farms, houses, and water. The world has no interactivity whatsoever aside from placing tiles in certain directions. 

There is no plot. 

[h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [6/10] [/b] [/h1]
The mechanics are deceptively simple - you get a random tile, and you place it on a map in a strategic position. The goal is to place tiles in a manner that completes the random quests that the game gives you. Things like having tiles with x attached houses or farms, or forests and also some small variants like not exceeding a specific amount so you can’t take advantage of a previous group of tiles, or things like closing off a section of tiles. Each completed quest then gives you more tiles so you can keep going for a bigger area and a higher score. 
To me, the gameplay loop almost felt like a simplified version of Tetris. Imagine if you had 5 shapes. Your goal here would be to combine the shapes into groups. Aaand that’s….kinda it. I think that while the quests and the pieces themselves offer some much-needed diversity in the gameplay through RNG, I felt there wasn’t a lot of meaningful interaction with the mechanics. 

As for the difficulty, this is generally a relaxing and chill game. Only when you care about getting higher scores can it become a test of patience as you realize you shouldn’t have placed that tile in that spot 5 turns ago. 

[h1] [b] Graphics (Quality/Technical) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
Simple and rudimentary. There’s not much here with graphics, each tile contains only a few variations of the same couple of biomes, so you’ll basically be seeing tiles with a combination of houses, forests, railroads, water, and farms, with the occasional special tile sprinkled in. Each tile doesn’t have enough detail for this the graphics to be good. 

On the technical side, I noticed no issues or bugs. The game ran smooth. 
i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | Windows 11 installed on SSD 

[h1] [b] Audio – [7/10] [/b] [/h1]
A great mix of relaxing and chill music to hex-out to. I thoroughly enjoyed how relaxing the music was. 

There is no voice acting. 

[h1] [b] Replay Factor (Longevity) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
I think the replay factor is there, but I can also see how it can be a tough sell. Yes, there are multiple game modes and the native RNG is actually a positive part of the game, but on the other hand, after only two or three games played I felt like I had pretty much seen all there was to see. The few games I played after that just felt repetitive. 

[h1] [b] Final Verdict – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
Dorfromantik is a charming puzzle game that caters to two very different play styles - a casual and relaxing vibe, and a hardcore score-chasing alternative. I think it meshes these two types of play styles pretty well, but I find myself being stuck in the middle. I like the relaxing vibe the game has, but its repetition has me bored. Meanwhile, I don’t want to invest dozens of hours learning the nuances just to compete on the leaderboards. It’s a strange feeling for such a chill feeling game. It’s almost like if Stardew Valley had a competitive MLG mode. Odd, right? 

Above in the mechanics section, I made the comparison to this game being kind of like Tetris, and I think it's a solid equivalency to both the strengths and weaknesses of this game. Like Tetris, the pieces you get are random, and you must fit them into a specific slot for max effectiveness. Also like Tetris, after playing only a couple of games, you’ve already seen pretty much everything the game has to offer from a gameplay standpoint. And also like Tetris, its simplicity is also its complexity as the skill floor is in the basement and the skill ceiling is ten stories high. 

Ultimately, do I recommend Dorfromantik? I think it’s a great game for mindless relaxing, but the game’s “mindless” aspect is incredibly boring to me. It’s like it pushes me into wanting to learn more and be better, when I find the core gameplay to be rather simple and repetitive. 
As you can probably tell, I’m a bit conflicted, and when I feel like smack in the middle, it's a solid 5 rating. In the end, I’m going to go with a recommendation because the casual approachableness of the game is worthy of checking out. 

[h1] [b] Recommend? (Price) [Y/N] [/b] [/h1]
[h1]Yes[/h1]
Base price of $14 is respectable. Sale price of $6 is a great price point.

Not sure why one the most popular tags for this game is "Relaxing", the game is actually stressful af 

The sheer anxiety that I get from thinking that there maybe was a better spot for this tile, I just couldn't find it. The absolute terror of watching the number of avaliable tiles slowly go down and realising that there's almost nothing you can do to replenish them. The anger that builds up inside me when I think: "No, not the fields tile again! Where the hell do I put it?!"

But I still love it

Probably the most anxiety-inducing game for anyone with OCD, but finding the ONE perfect tile placement that cascades into six other perfect placements is the most satisfying thing to do in this game.

I wish challenges and achievements weren't locked behind reaching the special tiles, or at least allowed us to preview them right at the start. These tiles can mess up hours of painstaking organization and waste even more tiles trying to reach them.
This is comfort in a game- a sit-down, brain-off experience that is perfect for winding down. Best enjoyed with a warm cup of tea after a long day.

Calming vibes, with the music and tones in the game.
TLDR; buy this game is you like easy going, go at your own pace, cozy, with optional puzzle element.

This is simple enough to start with, matching new pieces to existing tiles. The challenge comes bigger points requires bigger combos. The combos are matching sections, specific tiles, and longer chains. 

A charming piece of this game is how it generates new pieces for you to place as you advance. More charm is found when running long stretches of track or water, trains and boats appear. Oh, and windmills. 

Warning, it hard to resist finishing a round, especially when the stack of tiles gets low. The game also has a creative mode for you folks that want to lay out the perfect landscape.

In summary, great graphics, an enjoyable soundtrack, and cozy. Worth it at full price; goes on sale often.
Most chill game out there. Perfect for winding down after a stressful day or for a break at work.

Dorfromantik is a combination cosy puzzle game and city builder. Players build a landscape consisting of a variety of tile types through drawing and placing tiles on the map. Ideally, the landscapes on these tiles align with their neighbouring landscapes—forests touching forests, towns touching towns, etc.—though, due to the limited number of tiles and the existence of quests, there are incentives not to place tiles perfectly. Perfectly placed tiles, after all, yield more points, but fulfilling quests adds more tiles to the tile pile, creating a delicate balance between perfect placements, strategic tile placement, and aesthetic world design.

Because, to be clear, Dorfromantik is all about aesthetics.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3629747172 

Dorfromantik is very much a cosy city-builder. There is no time pressure, no imminent events, nothing that gets the heart racing beyond the diminishing pile of tiles (which, with good gameplay, refresh themselves with a satisfying regularity). Paired with this lack of pressure, though, is a soundtrack of calming little notes, adding a soft feeling to everything you do. The only sharp noise in the game is the chime of a perfect tile scoring. Tiles land with little pops, there are occasional rooster noises and bird song, but beyond that, there is nothing but the player and the soft music, serenading their careful world-crafting.

The visual design matches the music, with the map expanding into variously themed biomes, giving the world a sense of scale and each area its own feel, even while being clearly part of the same world. Rivers wend through cherry blossoms, spooky jack-o-lantern towns, and winter paradises before meandering their way out to the coast. Trains weave through endless forests, speckled here and there with cottages. Clocktowers and fountains dot the larger towns while the lights fade on and off in the small ones.

It's just...satisfying. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3629747697 

There are other cosy puzzle citybuilders that are mechanically better than Dorfromantik. Islanders, for example, does a better job of giving creative freedom, while 20 Minute Metropolis includes extra mechanics to make the game more of a puzzle. This is also not to say the game is flawless, as there is an inevitable frustration with running through my final ten tiles in search of the one that will let me actually continue the world. It is also not a game that lends itself well to more than one session at a time, though I’d argue that’s part of the point. Dorfromantik is escapism, but escapism that recognises that too much escape is just as dangerous as none at all.

Still, there is no game that hits the spot quite like Dorfromantik. When I load it up, I know I'm loading up a cosy hour or two. I know that, for that time, there will be me, and there will be the world, and there will be nothing else. It's an excellent way to destress and leave the real world behind. It is quintessentially cosy, and it is a quiet delight every time I play it.

Dorfromantic is an ostensibly chill game with the most frustrating progression/unlock system in any game I've ever played. To unlock new tile configurations and visual styles, you need to complete achievements, which are usually some form of tedium and/or rng dependence that will require you to play hundreds of games. That's an annoyance that other games have, but what makes dorfro so *special* is that by default, all your achievements are locked. You need to do a special challenge in a game, unlocking a fixed tile at the edge of the map and completing its quest, in order to unlock the ability to gain progress toward an achievement, one at a time. So you need to do the same thing hundreds of times to clear the achievement, but none of the times that you already did the thing count.

Why on God's green Earth is the game like this? What sadistic bastard thought it would be funny to force you to connect fixed tiles to unlock access to achievements one at a time, and had the balls to make one of those achievements require you to complete 50 more fixed tiles?

Maybe if you're looking for a time waster, you won't care that dorf is specifically designed to disrespect your time in innovative new ways. For me, considering how much they ask of your time to get what you paid for, I'm not convinced they should be asking the same of your wallet.

Dorfromantik is a beautifully crafted peaceful puzzle and city-building game that invites players into a tranquil, almost idyllic world where the primary goal is to create harmonious landscapes through tile placement. From the moment you start, the game exudes a calming atmosphere, emphasizing patience and creativity over speed or high-stakes competition. Its minimalist art style, characterized by soft pastel colors, charmingly animated scenery, and gentle sound design, fosters an immersive experience that encourages relaxation and mindfulness. The game’s aesthetic appeal is immediately apparent, and it manages to strike a perfect balance between simplicity and visual charm, making it accessible to players of all ages.

The core gameplay revolves around laying down tiles to extend a growing, interconnected landscape that includes fields, forests, rivers, villages, and railroads. Each tile you place must connect logically with existing terrain, creating a seamless and harmonious environment. The game introduces specific objectives for each level, such as completing a certain number of farms, forests, or villages, which adds a layer of strategic planning without feeling overly restrictive. As you progress, the game subtly guides you to think ahead, considering how each tile placement influences the overall landscape and future options. There's a soothing satisfaction in creating expansive, interconnected regions, and the game’s scoring system rewards thoughtful placement that maximizes harmony and coverage.

What makes Dorfromantik truly special is its emphasis on a meditative experience rather than traditional challenge or competition. The absence of time limits or aggressive constraints allows players to pace themselves, take their time to consider each move, and enjoy the process of landscape creation. The game also features a relaxing soundtrack composed of gentle melodies that complement the calming visuals, further enhancing the tranquil atmosphere. Occasionally, the game introduces new tile types or objectives to keep the experience fresh, but these are seamlessly integrated into the gameplay, maintaining the overall sense of calm and flow. The lack of intrusive UI or complex mechanics makes it easy for players to lose themselves in the serenity of the landscape-building process.

Dorfromantik also offers a sense of progression through unlocking new tiles, which are often tied to completing specific objectives or reaching certain milestones. This creates a subtle sense of achievement without detracting from the peaceful experience, encouraging continued exploration and experimentation. The game’s replayability is high due to its open-ended nature—players can craft new landscapes, experiment with different strategies, or simply enjoy the therapeutic act of tile placement. It’s a game that can be played in short bursts or extended sessions, making it perfect for moments of relaxation or mindful gameplay. Its gentle challenge lies in balancing expansion and harmony, inviting players to find their own rhythm and aesthetic in building their personal landscapes.

Overall, Dorfromantik stands out as a serene, charming, and deeply engaging experience that appeals to those seeking relaxation, creativity, and a break from the chaos of more intense games. Its elegant simplicity, combined with subtle strategic depth and a soothing atmosphere, makes it a standout title in the puzzle and simulation genres. Whether you're looking to unwind after a busy day or enjoy a meditative creative outlet, Dorfromantik offers a rewarding journey into a peaceful world of scenic construction and tranquil gameplay. It’s a testament to how a game doesn’t need to be complex or hectic to be profoundly satisfying and emotionally resonant.

[h1]Positive / Neutral / Negative[/h1]
+ Very relaxing game (sometimes too relaxing, so that I get sleepy :‘D)
+ Monthly themes increase the replay value
o I wish there were more clear objectives/quests, like in the actual board game
- Bigger maps can be quite chaotic/hard to navigate on a smaller screen

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Dorfromantik is a very cozy and relaxing game. 
You get a certain number of total tiles and need to build a map. It involves a bit of planning as not all tiles can be placed adjacent to each other. (The big exception are trains and river tiles. This is very well explained in the game tutorials though!) 
Cutting off your area, for example your forest, can end up in an early end if you cannot complete the objectives. 
I just wish there were a few more obvious quest lines available like in the board game. 
There are ingame achievements and feasts but I think they are not very obvious.

Dorfromantik also has replay value, as each month is a new theme available. 
Last month for example involved almost exclusively train and lake tiles, which made the game really complicated but fun! 

Oh btw, the controls on the Steam Deck are fine, but on bigger maps it tends to get a bit chaotic on the small screen. Especially if you have objects on different parts of your map. You may sometimes need to „jump“ a lot depending on which tile comes up next. By which I mean, scroll farther out, move around, scroll farther in, else moving over the map can be a bit slow. 

[h1]Visuals / Audio[/h1]
The visuals are very pretty. Later in the game, you are able to unlock several themes. My personal favorite is the [spoiler]Sakura Theme[/spoiler] and when I unlocked it, I immediately turned off all the other themes. I am really happy that this is an option in this game.
The background music is very chill and relaxing, which perfectly suits this game. I get cozy vibes whenever the music plays. A hot cup of chocolate, some very comfortable blanket and this game are a very good combination. 
Dorfromantik also has some sound effects, for example for the trains that are running through. They aren‘t very loud and are just proper fitting ambient sound effects. 

[h1]Performance[/h1]
Runs well on my Steam Deck. The bigger the map, and the faster you run from one edge to the other, it can result in tiny lags. They are not really noticable/an issue though. 
I did not adjust any settings. It just runs well on the default settings. :) 

[h1]Summary[/h1]
If you‘re looking for a relaxing building game with replay value, Dorfromantik may be an option! 
I will most likely get back to it occasionally, at least to do the monthly challenges, and whenever I need some relaxing time off.
good game, very calm and beautiful

7/10: Dorfromantik is a relaxing, low-stakes hexagonal tile placement game. Keep an eye on the remaining tiles and build towards the highest score you can muster!

Dorfromantiks soothing music and visuals make the game an excellent game to chill out with, or even play while watching something. The game session is limited by the number of tiles you have remaining rather than a time limit, but completing goals and sets nets you more so runs can continue for quite a while. The game lets you jump into and out of runs though, which makes it great either for a short session or for losing track of the hours as your world grows.

The tiles are charming, colorful places where each side of the hex could either contain a Dark Green Green Forest, Yellow Wheat Fields, Light Green Meadows, Water, Railroads, and more. Matching sides on tiles earns points, but the player must often choose between continuing to expand zones into larger areas or completing quests by closing off the zones they've built. There's achievements tied into pretty much each approach one might try though, some of which can take quite a while of tiling to accomplish. 

While it may not have an overarching narrative or test reaction times, what it does test is thoughtful planning and consideration of the goals you need to achieve. Getting record-breaking scores before running out of tiles takes an understanding of the games nuances that can turn short play sessions into multiple hours, while still allowing you to leave anytime you want without risking your play session.

I have been looking for something like this. A building game that is seemingly relaxing, beautiful, simple enough but a bit challenging. Dorfromantik is very close to all that, but some things about it can slowly turn relaxation to frustration and light challenge to a completely hopeless, impossible deadlock. I did enjoy the cheap game bought from the winter sale for a good while so I will recommend it but I will also share why you may not want to expect long term fun from this game (and how the owners could improve the game in case they want to).

The quest system is fundamentally flawed. This is what's supposed to allow you to sustain your game session and let you keep playing, awarding more pieces so you can continue to put down pieces. But sometimes the game just won't spawn quest pieces at all or they are all the same or completely irrelevant, so you lose no matter how well you planned and placed your pieces. It's a lottery. I want a game that rewards your efforts and let's you accomplish things. Lottery isn't that.

Even if you do get quests, every session is unsustainable by design (intentional I believe, not meant to go on infinitely but IMO it doesn't have to be like this). Your session will end regardless of your actions because the quest requirements always increase but the rewards for completion do not. In my opinion that's kind of a brain fart (big one) from the developers' side. As an imaginary comparison it's as if you'd get the same amount of money as a reward for every task completed but you'd always need to buy an ever-increasing amount things next. Every time more, but you always get the same reward. That makes it unrewarding and hopeless and it doesn't make you excited or even wanting to play the game further just to see your world end when you know you were doing everything right.

One more problem (or feature, because the game is intended to end I guess) is of course that every piece you get is completely randomized so very often they are completely useless. I already said I don't want a lottery but a game that I can succeed in if I just try enough. Surely a game developer can design better mechanics to challenge the player than to just hand them items they can't use. It just makes you feel like "This is bs" when you get dozens of pieces like that. Ones that simply do not fit well anywhere even if there are half a thousand spots.

So while the game may be designed and intended to end and not be continuous or infinite, I'm just saying I would better enjoy it if it wasn't like this. Like a game of pinball doesn't end until you mess up. There isn't anything new to be discovered either in a game of pinball, yet you feel the motivation and the desire to keep playing. I would like to feel that in this game too.

Dorfromantik is a serene and strategic tile-based puzzle game that encourages calm reflection and thoughtful planning. It offers a soothing experience, blending gentle gameplay mechanics with a relaxing atmosphere. Designed to reward creativity and foresight, the game provides an appealing escape from fast-paced genres. Its focus on tranquillity and progression gives it a distinct charm within the puzzle and strategy landscape.
Gameplay revolves around placing hexagonal tiles to build towns, forests, rivers, and railways in harmony. Each decision requires balancing short-term points with long-term potential, as the board expands organically with every move. The pacing encourages contemplation rather than haste, rewarding efficiency and spatial awareness. Its systems are simple to grasp yet layered enough to remain engaging over extended sessions.
Visually, Dorfromantik is beautifully understated, featuring soft colours and a charming, minimalist art style. The peaceful landscapes and smooth transitions between tiles enhance its meditative appeal. Gentle animations and ambient sound effects complement the visuals, reinforcing the overall sense of calm. Every element of presentation contributes to a cohesive and pleasing aesthetic experience.
Overall, Dorfromantik delivers a tranquil and rewarding puzzle experience that values relaxation as much as strategy. Its elegant simplicity and visual charm make it a standout title for those seeking a peaceful diversion. While it may lack narrative depth or high-stakes excitement, its soothing design and replayability ensure lasting enjoyment.
Dorfromantik gets a 7/10.

After a crazy day of work, nothing beats booting up Dorfromantik. It’s the ultimate "unwind" game, feeling less like a challenge and more like a necessary dose of therapy.

The first thing that hits you is the look of it. It’s absolutely gorgeous—the aesthetic is like a hand-painted miniature board game come to life, mixed with this cozy, low-poly charm. Watching the little trees grow into forests, the tiny trains chug along, and the houses cluster together into sprawling villages is pure visual bliss. Combined with the genuinely soothing, ambient soundtrack, it creates a true zen experience.

But don't let the cozy vibe fool you; beneath the picturesque surface is a deeply rewarding strategic puzzle. The challenge really ramps up because of the tile randomness. You constantly have to balance the urge to create a beautiful, perfectly enclosed forest with the strategic necessity of using a random tile to complete a quest for a huge lake on the other side of the map. It's a constant, fun tension between maximizing your score and indulging your inner landscape artist. You’re always one or two tiles away from either a brilliant score multiplier or a frustrating game-ending mistake, but the whole process is immensely satisfying and highly replayable.

Visually, the game is very appealing, and the music is great.  I play with the music turned down low, so I can hear it but it is not too intrusive. It is amazing how I can just sit and play for hours and hours.  You start with one tile, and you place a new tile each turn.  Before you know it, you have a huge map with hundreds of placed tiles!  

I like that when a game is done, they don't say "game over," or "you lose," but just "session complete."  As you get good at the game, you will appear on the leaderboard, and you can see your place even before you finish the game, based on your current score.
This game is very charming. I turn it on for five minutes here and there but often spend longer than I planned playing. You can easily spend far too much time playing by accident.
I also tried to commit slightly less genocide in this one and then I figured out it was not a dystopian citybuilder.

Easy to start a run with a few tiles and big plans, easy to leave it alone when the map gets too big to keep track of. Nothing amazing, but a good filler game when you have an indeterminate amount of time to waste in a pleasant setting.
Super chill game for when there is just not enough time for other games, or when your just feeling like creating a fun little town

I love this game. I turn to it often when I just need a little unwind. The soundtrack and gameplay are both very chill. Though sometimes I listen to my audiobook or music while I play it. It's low-stakes and very beautiful. Challenging enough, to encourage you to play again and again. The art is very soothing as well.
A really wholesome, beautiful-looking, chilled puzzle game. Because sometimes that's just what you need.
I love this cozy puzzle game. Very calming, no time pressure, and allows me to stop anytime (also mid-game) and proceed when i restart the game.

What a relaxing Puzzle game. This game is incredibly addictive and you can sink hours in without realising. My husband saw me playing this and was so enchanted he bought a copy and straight away sunk four hours into the experience. the fact that you can pop in and out of the game and just carry on is an excellent feature. I would highly recommend this to other people who are looking for a relaxing challenge.

Dorfromantik is solitaire. It's solitaire with an infinite deck of cards, but instead of cards you have hex tiles like you're playing settlers of cattan, or some other german board game with hexes. Does that sound fun? If so, play. If not, don't.

This game isn't for me, but it's so beautifully and passionately made that I simply can't help but recommend it. Loved every aspect of the gameplay, soundtrack, design and all, but - as I mentioned - it isn't for me.

This type of game is everywhere now, but I think Dorfromantik does it best. The different color schemes/themes are interesting and beautiful. The soundtrack is calming. The ability to control how you want to play is thoughtful and well executed. The achievements were difficult to achieve, but obviously not impossible.

The more you PLay the better it gets ,,***  Very relaxing and addictive*  Love the detail *** 
Cozy offline game to play.

I play it at work. Really easy to just flick in and out of. I've only played classic mode but there's a creative mode and a fair few other modes to get stuck into. Really nice looking game, that looks just as good in a small window the size of your email inbox as it does big screen. Unlocks come at a steady pace in the shape of tile skins. There's objectives to aim for as you expand. As everyone else has said, it's chilled, but you wouldn't be looking at the game if you were looking for CoD.
The vibe is soft, cozy and beautiful while the puzzle is engaging and ever changing. The music is lovely and allows for a calming experience.

It's beautiful, it's entertaining for a little while, but I've never really got hooked by it. I guess it's not that kind of game. What I'm trying to get at is... maybe I find it a bit boring. But that's because it's not my type of game, I can acknowledge how well crafted it is. And heavy discounted for 5 euros like I think I paid, then it's worth it.

Very chill game. Build countryside with fields, forests, villages, rivers/lakes, railways. Complete objectives to score points and add tiles to your dwindling stack. The tabletop version is pretty good too.
Fantastic little tile game.  Simple, casual, but a bit more depth if you feel like paying attention.

If you're looking for a game to unwind to, with no stress or impossible tasks, this is the game for you. Is a great way to just unwind and not have to focus 120% on competitive gaming. Would reccomend everyone have a game like this in their libary

This is a must have for your library! One of the best puzzle builders out there. The music is relaxing, the tile art is well thought out, and there are lots of achievements. Even at regular price, this game is worth it. These devs are 100% worth supporting!

This game might be my new favorite way to kill time. A solid puzzle game, rather relaxing AND a creative landscape builder all in one.

Games can be rather long if you play carefully, giving you ample time to build a little world you can be proud of. 
The landscapes can get a bit dull to look at if you play for too long a session.

Can you beat my high score of 27450?

Such a fun and cozy world building game, when you start with that one blank tile its hard to imagine the beauty that will sprout from it but by the time I was done with the tutorial I was enthralled. The different Biomes I discovered and skins I was able to freely unlock as the world unfolds around you in seemingly endless possibilities keeps me coming back to see what new things I can freely create.

Very nice puzzle game. Fitting the tiles is satisfying thanks to the quality sound and visual design. There is a distinct slow-burn challenge here which I found mildly fulfilling, but may be a little too slow for some. If you don't mind a solitaire game where you take your time and consider all the options between each move then you will probably find something to like in this lovely compact game.

A cozy game reminiscent of Photosynthesis, Carcassonne, and Settlers of Catan. Lay tiles, build out the country-side, fall into a relaxing flow with some great music and visual design. Perfect pre-bed game, so long as you don't get too sucked in to the flow.

I like low-energy strategy games that I can do while I'm working or when I'm feeling anxious that take up JUST the right amount of brain power. The soundtrack is excellent - I can play it while I'm in discord calls with other people without the audio being overwhelming or being too distracted. The art style is beautiful. And having so many different modes to choose and not being timed while creating really made this enjoyable. Highly recommend.
very chill game. very calming game. good puzzles, calming music, and overall a peaceful game. i highly recommend. dracotendo approved.
Great little puzzle game, super chill but also challenging as you get further through the game.
I love that this game is challenging, but still relaxing. The music is really nice, too.
Very chill, relaxing game that you can get lost in for hours or pick up just for a few moments
very relaxing and entertaining game and i love the developers kys
fun, satisfying and easy to play while blasting musicals

Cosiest of cosy games. No timers, no action, no stress. Perfect for someone like me who just wants to do some puzzles and build things. My only qualm is that we still don't have a mobile version. I just want to play this game on my iPad in bed. Please please please can you expedite the mobile version?

A very nice, relaxed game.  
Simple concept, relaxingly addictive.    
I agree with another reviewer, that there should be a way to bump up the stacks a little bit more easily, or wildcards or something.

Relaxing cozy puzzle game! Dorfromantik's gameplay formula is very simple, easy to understand, that becomes linearly more challenging the more you play it. The game looks like a city builder, but actually it plays more like a puzzle entry, one that requires strategy, thinking ahead, and a little bit of luck. The game sessions only come to an end when tiles run out, so the scope of every match is to aim for a high score. Aesthetically the game is very charming, with a colourful pallet and a sweet minimalist artsyle, one that enhances the gameplay. Dorfromantik is truly spendid!
Bought this game after playing the boardgame. It didn't dissapoint. Very relaxing.
Nice cosy game with a beautiful asthetic. if you just want to relax i heavily recommend this game.
Very chill puzzle game! Perfect to relax after a long day at work.

A very relaxing and zen-like strategy game where you place tiles with houses, fields, forests, water ways, and train tracks in a variety of ways to score points and unlock achievements. The game has an incredible balance of being laid-back and addictive, where running out of tiles gives you the tiniest pang of frustration before you inevitably start a new game.
Beautifully made game, tons of soul poured into it. Simple, yet very satisfying gameplay, perfect for a relaxing evening after work.

I will settle on a thumbs-up for this, but it is a fairly tepid one. It is very relaxing and at the end of each run you end up with a very pleasant-looking town, but the gameplay decisions really aren't that interesting. It's more of a relaxing unwind activity than a game per se (hence why I have so much time in it) but if that is what you're looking for this delivers.

Put a lot of lunch hours into this game. The art style is cute, the gameplay is simple - connect the same pieces together and expand the area. But that's what makes it addicting. Easy to pick up & play. Can easily spend hours playing it especially as you unlock new tiles.

This puzzle game is so wonderfully cute and satisfying! The simplest concept often equals the most fun games. 
I can spend hours on end in the Dorfromantik world and the monthly challenges gives some fun additions for re-play value. Highly recommend!
Very fun and relaxing, first game I ever played on steam, the 14 dollars I spent was worth it

Dorfromantik is the only game where I can spend hours lovingly curating a perfect little village, complete with flowing rivers, serene forests, and adorable towns, only to ruin the entire vibe because I accidentally rotated a wheat tile the wrong way and now it looks like Satan’s cul-de-sac. It’s basically digital zen gardening until you realize your quest for “optimal hex placement” has you sweating like you’re defusing a bomb. When the board finally clicks together and you’ve got the world’s most satisfying railway snake wrapping through it all, you’ll feel like Bob Ross reincarnated as a city planner. 10/10, my villagers deserve better leadership.

I slept on this game for years and decided to try this out thinking I may enjoy the board game. This is a very fun and relaxing puzzle game. I just keep coming back to it and am loving every second of it. The game is very simple draw and place hexagonal tiles with landscape or buildings on them. Joining like landscapes nets more points and some tiles come with objectives to connect say 500 trees or 50 houses. It took me maybe 5 games of wondering what the point was to be come totally hooked on this game and the level of calm and relaxation it provides due to the design and music is crazy. I will probably be getting the board game now too. Just a perfect puzzle game that is clearly elevated by being a video game.

Cozy, relaxing puzzle city builder... 
Absolutely great game when you want to just chill...
Very similar to the board game Carcazon.  It is fun, soothing.

This game is so satisfying and calming. I could sit and place tiles while listening to a podcast all day. My favorite cozy game right now. Would recommend to anyone looking for a low stimulus game to rot on.
Lots of fun, good way to relax ... until you start running out of tiles
Top tier cozy game! Even when I do poorly, the game doesn't feel like it's punishing me. Losing feels more like a chance to start fresh than a failure to play well, and scoring well feels FANTASTIC.
Cozy game that is easy to play even if I only have 15 minutes. Have enjoyed the diversity of the games and that it is not competitive. Highly recommend
It's a nice, calm game that stretches out your brain just enough to feel good. Not much else to say.
Chill vibes but deceptively tricky gameplay, and excellent game.
Fun and mildly relaxing game, all smoothly runs together, difficulty scales up quite quickly, quite a bit of rng

Great game, it has given me ample opportunities to train my thinking and is quite challenging for me in classic mode.
I hope one day Ill be able to reach a high rank in the leaderboard, otherwise very good!
I'm usually not one for puzzle games but this game is too easy to sink time into. Lots of fun learning the strategy but super relaxing
reminscent of villagers and for some reason, mini metro - gorgeous visuals and music, intuitive gameplay and an addictive loop. cant recommend enough!
This game is like an addictive smack in the face, that also makes you a cup of tea and offers you a biscuit.
Great game. Very cosy and relaxing, keep it up.
A nice and chilled game to just take mind of things . Gives brain something new to think about and plan where each tile should go . Music is so soothing to

This is a fantastic little time killer with a real soothing aesthetic and groovy soundtrack.  The issue I have with this game is that it requires too much patience.  I don't spend long enough thinking before I place my next tile, and it screws everything up.  If you want a game you can play for about an hour at a time to just unwind, this is a great option.

This is my go to relaxing game, there's no goal, no rush, no time limit, just... Place your tiles, create your little terrain. I could not be happier. I get lost for hours in this game and I can see myself coming back to it over, and over, and over again,
rules are super quick to pick up, was so good to play during covid

Simple and relaxing game.
pleasant to the eye and lovely soundtrack.
cute, meditative low-key puzzle game. good for listening to podcasts when too fatigued to craft

Very good game if you are not depressed. 

Best game ever if you are because you can play it in any mental state and it is very relaxing.
The game is easy to play and the visuals are pretty.  It's relaxing with just enough puzzle to keep it interesting.  It's also customizable, and there are different modes to try out.
So relaxing, easy to get in to, great for de-stressing, good milestones and achievements, love the sound design and music
One of those "easy to learn, hard to master" kind of games. I love the art style, the relaxing music, and even if I'm struggling with placement it's really hard to put down for long.
This is a lovely calm and no brain usage game. I love to play it in my downtime.
Really fun and relaxing game! Highly recommended! Once you play its hard to stop.

Very fun and relaxing. 
I thought it would get repetitive after a while, but it keeps you engaged with new buildings and idea's.
Perfect for a chill out sesh.
Its such a relaxing game, the soundtrack is lovely and I like how you can change the biomes :)

enjoyable whether you play it for the aesthetics or for the puzzle. challenging if you want it to be, not so easy that you don't TRY the puzzle... Super relaxing experience that I recommend to anyone who'd like Legos if they were hexagonal landscape tiles. The little animations are also very charming.

A truly relaxing game for when you just want to unwind.

Really helps if you're struggling with being a perfectionist - I find this game forces you out of that mindset in a nice way.

It's a joy just to mess about and try to keep playing as long as you can.

Great game, and cheap, too.

dorfromantik is a wonderful game if you're looking for something calm to play. if you want to 100% it, or you're trying to beat your high score? dorfromantik is tile hell. 10/10, would rotate my hexagons again

Dorfromantik is about as simple as a city builder can get. You place tiles. If you place tiles with houses together they become a "city." That's it. That's the gameplay. It isn't bad just much simpler than the term "city builder" implies. I returned it because it wasn't what I was looking for. But for someone who wants something very chill and relaxing without a lot of complicated systems or gameplay, then this is exactly what you're looking for. I can see why other people like it.
It is a cute little game. Totally worth its price tag.
Amazingly beautiful game. Perfect for when you wan to play something slow-paced but still have something with challenge in it. Also ridiculously addictive.

One of the most chill and relaxing games ever. The art is amazing and the music is so incredibly soothing. Dorfromantik is THE game to relax with. It can also provide great challenge if you want to hate yourself. Just go relax with the graphics and music.
Super cozy and relaxing game. You can play to try to optimize points and score big or just relax and build your land outward
I like that the game is challenging and you are constantly trying to find the perfect matching piece.
Cosy, relaxing but also challenging and very addictive.
Pretty relaxing little puzzle game with enough complexity to still challenge the mind a bit. Also gifted it to my non-gamer mom, who absolutely loves it.
Fantastic game, a nice and peaceful way to chill out and take some time for yourself away from the world.
Nice relaxing but still challenging puzzle game. Basically solo Carcassonne without the meeples.

Dorfromantik is one of those games that seems very chill and wholesome from the outset, then you have a panic attack because you are on your last 10 tile placements and the game refuses to give you the right railroad piece.

Still, it's genuinely nice and cozy. Works well if you want something low-energy to wind down with or if you want to stream something relaxing while chatting with your friends.
This is the perfect zen-out, sit back, and de-stress game for me. The music is very good at promoting a relaxing atmosphere.

Dang this indie game is a chill little work of art and raw human creativity! 

Beautiful little masterpiece. 

The music is reducing my stress and anxiety as we speak! 

Definitely gonna keep playing more of this.
Perfect game to play while watching a show without distracting from the show itself. Reminds me of the IRL boardgame Carcassonne but a bit more stripped down. Love the UI so much also.
It's a super chill game. I'd love to be able to rotate the upcoming stack of tiles to better match them to where I'd like them placed.

Relaxing Tile-Placer With a Strategic Twist. This game offers a simple and intuitive gameplay loop centered on tile placement. With soothing music and an engaging "Flag mission" mechanic, it draws players into a peaceful rhythm that makes hours slip by unnoticed. Fans of classics like Carcassonne, King Domino, or Akrotiri will likely feel right at home thanks to its familiar yet satisfying strategic elements.
relaxing and fun to play! i've come back multiple times and enjoyed hours of this game just passing the time - it's almost meditative. :)  the kids like it too
An interesting game for a casual game. At first, I found it a bit boring. But with each playthrough, my village grows larger, and the game becomes more fun.

Very fun game. More cozy-stimulating than actually relaxing, trying to position pieces effectively can really take some thinking and sometimes induce a bit of analysis paralysis. Good game for puzzle lovers.
A cute and cosy puzzle game. Highly addictive.
Soothing, endless - mostly, creative, satisfying!, excellent!
Love this game! So relaxing and fun that I lose track of time.

Beware of the time needed to carefully craft a map for one entire run. I did not focus at all on flags and perfect placement and my first took 2 hours till I capped... Its a very good concept, I would love this in other aesthetic style, Eras or Culture. Not a city builder but more then a zen solitaire.

Fun game, takes a little strategy to get high scores. I love that the pieces drawn are always very different. Can be frustrating when you don't draw what you need at the end, but it's literally luck of the draw and where you've established certain areas.
very fun, challenging, and beautiful puzzle game, its very easy to get lost in finding the perfect position for each hex

This game has considerably more depth than it looks. At first, it's a simple, relaxing game that gets old really fast. However, if you really try to reach high scores, then things suddenly get really difficult. You need to have strategy and have to pay attention of what to place and where. It might seem that getting over a few tens of thousands of points is impossible, there are people (not me) who'd got to the millions. It's possible, but it's difficult, even after reading a guide.

i love this game! the perfect chill and relaxing puzzle game. so visually appealing too. i can spend hours playing this by myself, or it's the perfect thing to play in the background while waiting for my turn in dnd. the soundtrack is AMAZING, i listen to it just for fun all the time.
great little cozy puzzle, very relaxing and chill

This may be the single most relaxing thing that I have on my Steam Deck.  It suits the Deck perfectly.  Engrossing and beautifully done.

The game essentially is dominoes, played on a hexagonal grid with matching in all directions, where the pattern of tiles in play builds an animated countryside village (Dorf) landscape.
Super relaxing and fun game! I love all the different game play types, it's also great for creating little fantasy maps.

I didn't like this game at first.  I actually uninstalled it after a few hours but past the refund point and it just sat for a couple years.  I decided to give it another shot and glad I did.  I'm pretty hooked now!
Very easy to grasp from the beginning. Soothing and relaxing while also being challenging. Different playing options to keep things fresh.

I've played this game so many times! It's one of my favourite games!

It's the perfect game for when you are exhausted but cannot sleep. It has a very simple gameplay: just position the next tile in a favorable way and try to get points. It can be a very chill and meditative experience, especially if you are not a maximizer by nature and let yourself just flow with the serene soundtrack and pretty images.
so cozy, amazing art style, infinitely replayable. one of the best puzzle games on the market!

Super relaxing, and beautiful to look at, but still a stimulating enough puzzle that it doesn't get boring. I also love going into the creative mode after I've finished a regular playthrough, to tweak and add things that are just aesthetic.
Great game for a quick session in between. Also has this dangerous loop: Just one more round.

This game is my happy place.

Whenever I feel stressed out, whenever stuff goes sideways, playing this for an hour or so always calms me down and re-centers me. The no-stress gameplay, the awesome soundtrack, the little dopamine hits whenever I complete a tile set, the big dopamine hits when I clear a forest with six flags...just lovely and soothing.

Maybe it'll do that for you too.

boring Zoom? Dorfromantik. boring class? Dorfromantik. bad day? Dorfromantik. this is one game that never needs me to be more than I am or do more than identify a hex type and see where it will match best. it is aesthetic. it is kawaii. it is uwu. it is for the depresso girliepops (gender neutral) that just want something, anything, in life, to *be beautiful and fit.* and in the world of Dorfromantik everything does, on a scale of 0-perfect, in a stack of (never)ending hexes. welcome to a world where you will have a favorite tile type for the bears.
soothing, catan-esque, puzzle solving creative game. audio and visuals great for folks looking for a calm world building point and click experience.

This is probably one of the most relaxing games I have ever played.  I use it to reduce daily stresses, and it's strangely meditative.  Definitely recommended if you are looking for a game to chill out and play while on conference calls, streaming content, or just wanting to play something that doesn't involve blowing stuff up, gathering resources, FOMO promotions, or any of the other trappings of modern gaming.

Chill game to play from time to time. You don't have to be mad about optimizing to build a city. 

But, to build a good city, hot damn.

perfect game for playing while voicechat with pals
完美适合一边和朋友聊天一边玩的游戏
It is insane how addictive this game is! It's a simple little concept but really tough to master. One of these days I'll have the perfect game lol

Why haven't I reviewed this yet? I have sunk a lot of hours into and, yet no review? Why? Anybody know?

Oh, and the game is great etc, but I really do not think my review will help you figure out if you will love it. So lets focus on why I have not review this before.
Near perfect game. Relaxing but challenging if you want it to be. Good variations in game modes and very consistent in design. Overall very satisfying and great for perfectionists.

I have ADHD and OCD and this game helps me relax. 
It keeps my brain occupied enough to think properly without getting distracted, and I get rewarded when every edge lines up perfectly.
Love to boot this up and throw on a podcast or audiobook. Great game to play to wind down for the night.

I have barely scratched the surface of this game but I can say that this is going to be my new go-to game for relaxing. Each round feels like a perfect session to play and the only complaint is that I can easily lose track of time even with one round.

Pretty much the perfect chill game, with an arcade scoring system that has it's HOOKS in me. Just the right combination of RNG and strategy, every game goes slightly better than the last because I'm getting better at planning and being flexible. And that also makes me immediately want to play again. 

Let me put it this way. Elden Ring Nightreign just came out, and I have a Dark Souls tattoo on my leg. Despite this, I cannot put Dorf Romantik down.
Amazingly relaxing puzzle game where you create little worlds with the tokens earned by making good choices with prior tokens.

Dorfromantik is a tile-based city builder that's a bit like a cross between a jigsaw puzzle and chess. It's very relaxing and methodical like doing a jigsaw, but there's also strategy and thinking ahead involved if you'd like to chase a high-score. The music is calming and the atmosphere pleasant, with nice sound effects and feedback animations. It's a simple game that will increase in play time as you get better, however can start to feel a little repetitive during longer games. It's a good game to play with a cup of tea after a long day, just for a round or two. Nothing mind-blowing, but great when you're either anxious, worn out, or low on brainpower...or if you just enjoy puzzles : )
Great game to pass the time. I play it while listening to audiobooks or podcasts. It helps me remember what I hear. I also use it to relax during short breaks.

Nothing to say about the game other than Amazing! 
A game that looks easy at first, but involves a decent amount of thinking.
Always fun to come back to, looks amazing and also gives you a nice inspiration to unintentionally build very organic landscapes which you can use as a template for other creative projects

This is a wonderful and thoughtfully made game. The art is beautiful to look at and the game play is challenging but fun in all the best ways. I've only played for a short while so far, but I definitely see myself sinking many hours into this game in the future.
I chose this game, because of being chill, reminded me of Carcasone and could be played only by mouse. And it was amazing to play.

I adore everything about this game. I works so smoothly, the music is lovely and adds to the whole atmosphere, the art style is charming, the colour scheme is calming and the rogue-lite elements mean that I could play this game endlessly!
HIGHLY addictive and very enjoyable. Very pleasing stuff.

Such an adorable passive game. I enjoyed playing this while making phone calls to keep my hands and eyes busy and appreciated that it requires some attention, but not my full attention. The graphics were adorable and continued to provide little surprises along the way to keep things engaging.
Relaxing Game! Tons of fun for all puzzle solvers and satisfying when you get all tiles lined up. The animations are good fun to watch as your creation gets bigger. Recommend highly!

Dorfromantik is a cute little sandbox game great for when you need time to unwind. Most of the fun of playing this for me is the way it makes you think and strategise while also being relaxing at the same time. Pretty fun game, would get

If its the only thing you are doing and you are the kind of player that enjoys fast paced games you are gonna refund in an hour at best. And if you are the kind of player that likes strategy games deep games you will also get bored. So if you want something casual you can do while listening or watching to something that's your game.

Sometimes you just want to play a relaxing, casual game. This is one of those games. There is a scoring system but really it's fun to just build a little town with your hex tiles and watch it animate. Love the style, love the gameplay, love the music and the sound effects.

Cozy little game which I currently suck at, but it's still fun to place tiles listening to the gentle soundtrack.

You can play it as little or as much as you prefer, there are different game modes, including a sandbox one, so you don't have to stress.

Get it, enjoy it.
Perhaps the perfect game. Could only be better if they released more tilesets.
after playing similar board games lining up tiles I started to look for a game like that and this is that its amazing

I love this game <3
Nice and relaxing gameplay, which lets you take your time to build beautiful landscape while listening to chill music.
Addicting! I like that it makes you have to think about placements. It's a fun relaxing little puzzle game.

Addictive in its simplicity.  To ticking time, no competition.  Just you and a bunch of hexagonal map tiles.  Finish quests to get more tiles and keep going.  Beautiful graphics blend with blissfully relaxing background music and gentle animal noises.  This is my new go-to relaxing mindless strategy game- After a long, stressful day, I just spent two and a half hours playing and came away feeling relaxed and eager to play even more.  I cannot recommend this game enough.

This is a fun puzzle game.

If you are playing it "just chill and play with the tiles" it can be relaxing. 

If you are playing it to beat the challenges and achievements it will take some effort.

Extremely relaxing puzzle game! Don't get me wrong, it is difficult to obtain all tiles and thus achievements, but unlike other games, it doesn't feel too tedious. A very nice game when you want to breath a bit!
neat little game, it's calming and chill game, follows a simple concept but with enough room for planning/strategy that it makes it feel rewarding
Dorfromantik is such a beautiful and peaceful puzzle game, I love it! A fabulous way to relax.

Good for 5 - 10 hours of relaxing puzzle-like fun. Wouldn't recommend paying more than $10 for it.

Gets a bit samey pretty quickly. The RNG nature of the tiles makes it a bit annoying to plan; it is difficult to create a map that looks as well put together as the promo images/videos.
simple, fun and addicting. I absolutely recommend this game.
Immediately accessible and provides great replay-ability.  I loved it so much I got all the board game variations.  Oh, and the soundtrack is outstanding.

Wonderfully zen puzzle game. The principles are simple, but every game is a little different, and every time you learn new things about how to best strategize, get more points, etc. Relaxing, very visually appealing, very well made. Highly recommend.
Mellow puzzle game, meditative, beautiful. Choose how careful you want to be, or if you just want to build.
it's relaxing, and keeps hands and mind busy
Super addicting puzzle game. So good it got an unofficial sequel!

It would me great if patterns for mixing different lands were not so strange (not random, so you can never get a tile to fit your unique place). 

No strait possibility to set difficulty level - so instead of relax you will get frustration than it grows.
Cute game to pass the time. Very pretty landscapes and interesting challenges.
Pretty cute and relaxing game. Low stakes builder that never stops being engaging.

I was looking for a game to unwind in the evening and this is a perfect fit. The interface is intuitive, the game play is pretty easy to learn but is still challenging to get good at. The graphics and sound are a perfect fit for the vibe. Thank you for making this game! It's exactly what I was looking for!

cute, good, fun little puzzle game that challenges your ability to remember patterns and shapes to get higher scores. you might find yourself pleseantly surprised by its charm, and its challenging yet simple design.
A very cosy and relaxing game to play.  Would thoroughly recommend.
It's a soothing game that I really enjoy after a long or stressful day.

So relaxing, visually pleasing, and it never gets boring. This game does everything right. I can't think of anything bad to say. Been playing for years and I still love coming back to it. Dorfromantik – A Peaceful Puzzle Masterpiece - ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)

Dorfromantik is the kind of game that sneaks into your heart with its serene charm and keeps you coming back for “just one more tile.” It’s a beautifully simple yet deeply engaging puzzle game where you build picturesque landscapes one hexagonal tile at a time. There’s no stress, no enemies—just a relaxing flow of city-building and puzzle-solving that soothes the soul.

🏡 Gameplay:
You start with a stack of tiles, each containing a mix of forests, rivers, fields, villages, and railways. Your goal is to place them strategically to complete objectives and extend your run. The mechanics are easy to grasp, but as you play, you start to appreciate the subtle depth—maximizing points, creating sprawling cities, and crafting scenic landscapes that feel uniquely yours.

🎨 Visuals & Atmosphere:
Dorfromantik’s soft pastel colors and charming, minimalist design make it a joy to look at. Watching your world grow from a few scattered tiles into a living, breathing countryside is incredibly satisfying. The gentle music and ambient sounds (birds chirping, water flowing) add to the cozy, meditative experience.

⏳ Replayability:
With different game modes, including a creative mode that lets you build without restrictions, there’s plenty to keep you coming back. Whether you’re chasing high scores or just enjoying the act of creating something beautiful, Dorfromantik delivers endless charm.

🎯 Final Verdict:
If you love relaxing puzzle games, city-building, or just need a break from fast-paced action, Dorfromantik is a must-play. It’s a game that invites you to slow down, unwind, and enjoy the simple pleasure of creation. Highly recommended!

👍 Perfect for: Cozy gamers, puzzle lovers, and anyone looking for a peaceful escape.

Great game, excellent all-round - except the achievements.

The Rewards/Achievements system is unique, but I don't think it works well. Most achievements are incredibly grindy, super time-consuming and wholly unrewarding, and don't drive the player towards fun with the game or to learn its mechanics deeper (as well-designed achievements do), but drive the player towards repetition, boredom, and sub-optimal play. Some achievements are unearnable until they're unlocked through play as "Challenges" - which is an interesting idea I haven't seen before. But primarily you have three on-screen achievement goals that seem to be random, and you can't unlock any of others that aren't the three on-screen. I rolled really unfun grindy ones in particular, it seems.

Achievement design in games is often overlooked and misunderstood. I respect this game for introducing me to some new ideas for gate-kept achievements and on-screen achievement goals, I've never seen that before - but unfortunately I don't think the innovation paid off. I think the Rewards/Achievements system actively detracts from the game experience, as all badly designed achievements do - encouraging or directing players to less fun modes of play, and greatly decreasing intrinsic motivation to play and experiment with a game. Dorfromantik in particular incorporates its achievements into the base game HUD UI always on-screen and ties its achievements deeply with gameplay, making it hard to ignore. This is definitely the most an achievement system has ever detracted from a game's basic gameplay loop and standard play experience for me.

Dorfromantik would probably be close to a 5/5 for me, being a near perfect version of the exact game it was trying to be, but honestly the achievements system guts the play experience so bizarrely much for me, I'd drop to a 3/5. Still a good game. But it would legitimately be more fun if the achievements were just completely removed - which is a rare trait among games.
